title: What would be the best genre of game to make on RM( MV )?

posts.author: ThatIndieSphinx
posts.body:
First of all, I would just like to clarify what I mean by 'best'.
I see a lot of games made with RM that aren't actually RPGs, like horror, and I was wondering which genre would be the most popular, but also easy to make?
Obviously, I could learn how to code and script a 3D FPS shooter game, but that would be unrealistic for me
because I am bad at coding that's why I used RM
. I am aiming for a balance between easy to make and able to gain recognition.
Ideally, it would be a genre that does not require heavy use of plugins.
Note: sorry if I posted this in the wrong forum, I didn't really know where this would fit in.

posts.author: SGHarlekin
posts.body:
I believe those two are are mutually exclusive. You're not going to make an easy to make game and gain recognition. You're trying to get into an industry that is oversaturated to the brim with every genre imaginable. And industry that is pure luxury. Any sort of slop will not gain you recognition. In fact, most even decently made games will not gain you recognition.
What gains you recognition is making an outstanding game. (Look at the recent example Hollow Knight: Silksong. Made by a team of 3 over the span of about 9 years.)
You're competing with professionals that spent years of their life honing their craft with "What's an easy to make genre?" in a market that has more games than anyone can play in their lifetime.
Even if you take one of the easier to produce genres like a walking sim story game, you'd need to be an exceptional writer with stunning visuals to achieve any sort of recognition. There is no way you're going to pull that off with your run off the mill rpg maker assets and from this what it reads like "get rich quick" attitude.
Instead of trying to achieve fame, a better approach, and probably what most of us are doing, is to just make the games you want to make with features you'd like to see in a game.

posts.author: ZombieKidzRule
posts.body:
Welcome to the forum!
Not to be that Zombie, but an RPG is just any Role Playing Game. So, a horror game can absolutely be an RPG. Heck, you could make a Visual Novel type game an RPG depending on how you approached it.
With that said, I would say the "best" game for any developer would be the game that is something they can actually finish within their own skill set and within the limitation of the engine.
I wouldn't personally try to make a 3rd Person shooter, Skyrim replica, or even an involved platformer in MV or MZ. Not that I haven't seen some platformer games mind you.
But you can do a lot without plugins. I'm making a Sudoku game with only a couple of default plugins and a couple of small custom plugins that folks here in the community were kind enough to help me with.
You can make a "traditional" RPG Maker looking game without any plugins if you want. It really depends on what you want to do.
I also agree with the point that I don't think anything that would be considered "easy to make" would be likely to help you "gain recognition". It really depends on your interpretation of what is "easy" and how much work you are willing to put into it.
Or, you could "gain recognition" is a way that you don't want.
If you have never finished an actual game before, I would strongly recommend making a very simple, short game to help you gain experience with what it actually takes to complete a project. Then you could look to expand based on your new found knowledge.
Perhaps most importantly, I would suggest picking something that you would want to play and that will keep your interest.
But I don't really think there is necessarily a "best" type of game to make in RPG Maker unless you consider the "straight out of the box" type of game that RPG Maker was obviously marketed for as being the "best" and "easiest". But that type of game can also lead to being quickly labeled as "shovelware" which is not the type of recognition that is desirable.
Regardless, good luck on your projects and remember to enjoy what you do!
EDIT: Also, don’t sell yourself short. Your profile says you are pretty young. I didn’t start learning RPG Maker or learning JavaScript until about 3 years ago when I was in my 50s. You can learn to do a lot if you are willing to give it a try.

posts.author: JohnDoeGames
posts.body:
Uhm... Just saying, there are genre's and genre's. You have game genre's like: RPG, FPS, Side scroller, platformer, simulator, etc etc. And you have genre's like: Romance, horror, comedy, drama, etc etc.
One is about the gameplay, the other is about the story, the theme and the ambiance. And pretty much every game genre, can have any story genre you like. And RPG can be a horror, or romantic, or a drama. Platformers too, and simulators.
You ask for a FPS... Well, even though I've seen it done with RPG maker, it isn't the best game genre to choose for RM. It is hard, it is complicated and it will not be a smooth as the fps's you've been playing. That doesn't mean you should only make RPG's with RM. Puzzle games and strategy games and simulation games and... and... even platformers. It can all be done with RPG maker with ease.
If you really want to make an FPS in RM, you should look at MV3D, which is a plugin. It turns the 2t topview game into a 3d game. It is a bit complicated for a beginner and it isn't free either, but it will give you the opportunity to make a full 3d version of your game.
Turning it in a shooter, however, that is a whole different story.

posts.author: JohnDoeGames
posts.body:
AquaEcho said:
RPG Maker is specialized for making a turn-based grid-based RPG or "walking sim". For every other genre there is a better, easier, and faster engine to make it in.
Click to expand...
I don't think I agree on that... I made card games, a chess game and board games, which even today I wouldn't be able to recreate without RPG maker. (And yes, that is because I know so much about MV and nothing about any other engine...)
It is just a lot easier to master everything RPG maker has to offer than it is to master a fraction of Unreal or PixelGameMaker or GoDot or... Any of the engines I tried.
If you really know nothing about game development, then RPG maker is by far the easiest one to learn it. I just think a FPS shouldn't be your first project.
My advice: Create a game with the engine as it is intended first, and try out every single function there is in the engine. Doesn't matter if it makes your game better or ruins it all, just try it. Your first game is going to suck anyway, that is fine, you're learning.
Once every single button and parameter in the engine is understood and you know exactly how you can use each and every one of them, you can make anything you want. I wanted to have a card game, so I made a ton of "Show picture" and "move picture" commands to have cards go from one position to another.
Going from top-view to first person is one of the few things I wouldn't be able to do without plugins. Luckily those plugins exist, like FPLE or MV3D for MV.

Construct and GDevelop already have templates for chess and various card games. I am recommending those engines specifically because they are no code, have more users than RPG Maker (thus community resources and help), and praised by their own users as being very easy and fast to churn out games with. They are also both general purpose engines that have tools built in to handle a wide variety of genres.
Pixel Game Maker has a learning curve, a small user base (meaning less community help) and GGG doesn't support it any more because they moved on to Action Game Maker. Godot and Unreal require code.

posts.author: Eternidade_1
posts.body:
I believe the best RPG maker game is one that's creative, beautiful, fun, and interesting. Furthermore, you need to play the game to form an opinion; reviews from other users alone aren't enough to define someone's taste for a game.
Bad games are those that use more of the same, without depth. I'm not talking about game genres, but rather a lack of innovation.
As for what you should create, it should be a current genre that has market traction. You can compare the Beat 'em up genre to something old and focus on newer genres like
Roguelikes/Roguelites: Focused on exploration and incremental progression with each new game (Hades, Dead Cells).
Soulslikes: Challenging, with an emphasis on strategic combat and subtle narrative (Hollow Knight, Elden Ring).
Survival Horror: Where scarcity of resources and suspense are key (Resident Evil, Silent Hill).
Metroidvania: Focused on exploring a large, non-linear map, with abilities that unlock new areas (Ori and the Blind Forest).
The most recommended genres to start with are:
Puzzle Games
These are considered the easiest for beginner developers. The complexity isn't in the code or graphics, but in the level design and puzzle logic. Once the core mechanics are working, you can reuse them across all levels, simply by changing the setting and the order of the challenges.
Visual Novels
If your greatest strength is writing, this is the ideal genre. The main focus is on the story, dialogue, and static art. You don't need a complex combat system, physics, or elaborate animations, which drastically reduces development time.
Simple Adventure Games (Top-Down)
Genres like detective games or top-down exploration games (like classic RPGs) are great. Movement is simple, and challenges can be based on finding items, talking to characters, and solving mysteries, which puts the focus on the creativity of the story and world.
Finally, if I were to create something like this based on genre, I'd create a Visual Novel, which is quite beautiful and allows you to implement several different mechanics, highlighting its full potential.
